items.title: Father Al Lewis Interview, 1972-02-21
items.q: when you're a trooper up and down the road like I was, like Alvin Walz and the bands like that, you run into everything.

ctx.x: The big fat guy that played trombone, outside of his mouth.

He's playing on that number I played a while ago, Someday You'll Be Sorry with Lewis Armstrong and all the bone. Yeah, well that guy man. Sure, you see, when you're a trooper up and down the road like I was, like Alvin Walz and the bands like that, you run into everything. You run into everything. And the guy is just another member, you know, who turns your brother, and they sit in there and play.

I'll tell you a nice guy to meet, or see him in the business, Charlie Barnett. Yeah. Do you know, I was talking to Captain Hattie, have you heard that tape? And he told about the jam sessions where Ross Barnett would come and play Stockton's song? Yeah. Yeah. Not Ross Barnett. Yeah. That was the governor of Mississippi. I know, yeah. But he got Charlie Barnett and Ross Barnett. Yeah, he was mixed up, yeah.
